source: NCERT Class IX, Contemporary India I, Geography Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The Making of Indian Landforms
points: Landforms result from movement of **lithospheric (tectonic) plates**.
The **Himalayas and Northern Plains** are the most recent (young); the **Peninsular Plateau** is the oldest, most stable landmass (part of ancient **Gondwana**).
India has **six** major physiographic divisions.

sections.heading: 2. The Himalayan Mountains
points: **Young fold mountains** in the north; run west–east.

sub: **Himadri (Great/Inner Himalayas)** — highest, permanent snow; has **Mt Everest, Kanchenjunga**.

points: Divisions west to east: Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal, Assam Himalayas; the **Purvanchal** (eastern hills).

sections.heading: 3. Northern Plains and Peninsular Plateau
points: **Northern Plains** — formed by **alluvium** of the **Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra** systems; very fertile. Old alluvium = **bhangar**; new = **khadar**.
**Peninsular Plateau** — old crystalline rocks; two parts: the **Central Highlands** (north of the Narmada) and the **Deccan Plateau** (south).
Bordered by the **Western Ghats** (higher, continuous; highest peak **Anai Mudi**) and **Eastern Ghats** (lower, broken).
The **Aravalis** (NW) are among the oldest mountains.

sections.heading: 4. Desert, Coasts and Islands
points: **Indian (Thar) Desert** — west of the Aravalis (Rajasthan); arid; the **Luni** is the only large river.
**Coastal Plains** — the **Western Coastal Plain** (narrow: Konkan, Kannad, Malabar) and **Eastern Coastal Plain** (broad: Northern Circar, Coromandel); large deltas on the east.
**Islands:** **Lakshadweep** (Arabian Sea, **coral**) and **Andaman & Nicobar** (Bay of Bengal; **Indira Point** = southernmost point of India).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Six divisions: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands.
Himalayan ranges: Himadri (highest) > Himachal > Shivaliks (Duns).
Northern Plains = alluvium (Indus/Ganga/Brahmaputra); bhangar (old) vs khadar (new).
Western Ghats (continuous, higher, Anai Mudi) vs Eastern Ghats (broken, lower); Aravalis = oldest.
Lakshadweep = coral (Arabian Sea); Andaman & Nicobar (Bay of Bengal); Indira Point = southernmost.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Himalayan ranges N→S: **Himadri → Himachal → Shivaliks**; **Duns** are in the Shivaliks.
The **Peninsular Plateau is the oldest** landmass; the **Himalayas are young**.
**Western Ghats** are continuous & higher (Anai Mudi = highest); **Eastern Ghats** are broken & lower.
**Lakshadweep = coral islands (Arabian Sea)**; Indira Point (Andaman & Nicobar) is India's southernmost point.
